newsitem.title: INDIA: India's Jindal sees cash flow improving.
newsitem.headline: India's Jindal sees cash flow improving.

text.p: Indian steel maker Jindal Strips Ltd expects its cash flow to improve considerably in coming months due to a lower than expected response to a share put option, the company said on Monday.

"The response to the scheduled put option is lower than what the company had provided and planned for. As a result, the company will not need to stretch beyond its means in the coming months," corporate finance vice-president Arvind Parakh said in a statement.
In 1993 the firm raised $60.5 million in convertible bonds, due to mature in March 1999. About $10 million were converted into equity shares with a put option valid until February 1997.
"Over the last month, Jindal Strips has received options to the extent of $32.34 million only, thereby gaining from the reduced redemption requirement," the statement said.
It quoted Parakh as saying that the $32.34 million would be financed through internal accruals and better cash and inventory management.

Jindal, India's only integrated manufacturer of stainless steel, said a proposed decrease in import duty on nickel would also improve its performance. Nickel constitutes about half of the raw material cost incurred in making stainless steel.

"This is expected to have a positive impact on the profitability of the company in future years. Additionally, the international steel market has rebounded with prices on an upswing by five to eight percent," the statement said.
